title: Payoff Desk Guide, Retail Installment Contracts: Review Days for a Recently Returned Channel
content:
A borrower payoff of a contract under Retail Installment Contracts carries returned-channel review days read from the contract's latest return — the return with the latest return date, and among returns of the same date the one recorded first — and the channel of the payment that was returned.

**Rule.**

- When the latest return is dated in the rolling 12 months ending on the posting date and came through an ACH channel — a recurring autopay draft, a one-time self-service bank draft or a one-time bank draft taken by a representative — **2** review days are added.
- When it is dated in that period and was a mailed personal check, **4** review days are added.
- Otherwise none are added.

| Latest return | Original channel | Review days |
|---|---|---|
| dated in the rolling 12 months | ACH (autopay, self-service draft, representative draft) | 2 |
| dated in the rolling 12 months | mailed personal check | 4 |
| dated in the rolling 12 months | debit card or any other channel | none |
| dated before the rolling 12 months | any | none |
| no return on the contract | — | none |

The rolling 12 months run from records dated later than the same calendar day 12 months before the posting date (the last day of that month when that day does not exist) through the posting date. Only the latest return is read: an older mailed-check return does not count when a later return exists.

**Hypothetical case (posting date 6 October).** A mailed check returned on 7 October of the previous year, and no later return: inside the window, 4 days. The same return dated 6 October of the previous year: not later than the 12-month mark, none.
